p.span: Ms STEPHANIE DI PASQUA ( Drummoyne ) ( 17:16 :03 ): For 49 years, the Labor Party held the electorate of Drummoyne. For almost half a century, successive Labor local members had the opportunity to deliver infrastructure, services and investment for my community, and they did not. In 2011, when my community elected a Liberal representative, that changed. Since 2011 the people of Drummoyne have seen significant investment in their schools, hospitals, transport infrastructure, parks and community facilities. I take this opportunity to put some of that Liberal investment on the parliamentary record today, because it matters who planned those projects, funded them, fought for them and, importantly, ensured that they were delivered.

Let us start with health. The former Liberal Government committed $341 million to stage one of the major redevelopment of Concord hospital. That included the National Centre for Veterans' Healthcare, the first of its kind in Australia; the new Concord Cancer Centre facility; new aged-care and rehabilitation wards; and more beds. That investment delivered modern health facilities, the first of their kind at Concord hospital, and supported the future of the hospital, which is one of Sydney's most important and busiest hospitals. The Concord hospital multistorey car park was also planned and funded by the former Government. I am proud to have advocated to ensure that that project was continued and delivered by this Government, because anyone who has visited Concord hospital knows just how important the accessible parking is.

That major master planning work for Concord hospital was done by the former Liberal Government. The master plan is there. Our community wants to know: Where is the funding for stage two? Where is the commitment? Where is the plan? After almost four years of a Labor government, we have not seen a single dollar for the second part of the Concord hospital upgrade—a new emergency department—all while the Government is adding more than 60,000 new homes in our community. I will also talk about education. Under the former Liberal Government, our electorate benefited from substantial investment in local schools, including three new and upgraded schools: Russell Lea Public School, Victoria Avenue Public School in Concord West and the total knockdown and rebuild of Lucas Gardens School.

It also included the major upgrade to Concord High School, with 40 new classrooms. Planning for that was done by the former Government. When I became the member, I met with the Concord High School principal, who said to me, "It's all on pause. It's all being held up. We don't know what is happening now that we have a new government." That project is particularly important to me. I am proud to have advocated on behalf of my community for the delivery of Concord High School. The same principle applies to Rhodes Public School. When a government completes a project that was planned and funded by its predecessor, it is only right that that history should be acknowledged. The public record should be accurate. Rhodes Public School has been held up by Labor. For three whole years, there was not a single update on the Department of Education website about Rhodes Public School. When the community and I started asking questions about that, all of a sudden we saw an announcement. I will always welcome investment in my community, but let us be fair dinkum and honest about who planned and funded Rhodes Public School.

Our community has also benefited from public transport, which was made more accessible by the former Government. All of our rail stations, including at Rhodes, North Strathfield and Concord West, were updated to include lifts. Further, all of our ferry wharves, including at Drummoyne, Abbotsford, Chiswick and Cabarita, were made accessible. I note that when those works were being done, replacement services and interim arrangements were organised. That is why people in my community are so upset about the closure of Abbotsford ferry wharf for approximately two months. No practical transport replacement arrangements were made and there are no express services from Chiswick during that time. I note the Minister for Roads is present in the Chamber. I ask her to listen to the frustrations of my community and act on them. My community was given a short notification. The Government knew about this for a year but said and planned nothing. I hope the Government delivers replacement bus and ferry services for my community.

Ms JENNY AITCHISON ( Maitland—Minister for Roads, and Minister for Regional Transport) (17:21:09): I want to set the record straight. I am advised that replacement bus services started at 6.00 a.m. this morning, so buses are in place. Let us also look at why that work needs to be done. When that wharf was replaced by the former Government in 2018, it was supposed to last for another 25 years, but it did not quite make the distance. Transport for NSW had to step in and fix the gangway, again. It had to fix the former Government's shoddy workmanship. It would be nice to get a thank you from the member for Drummoyne—she is welcome—for the work we have done in her electorate after a failed infrastructure upgrade from 2018 under the former Government. The member may be very proud of what the former Government did, but she should own her mistakes.
